business_scope: local IM input requirements, local sequential record only; no network, identity verification, durable storage, device delivery or read acknowledgement
prerequisites: 01.02 scalar values, string byte length, comparisons
01.03 first-pass branches, ordinary functions and multiple returns
first_pass: Clarifying ambiguous business requirements into explicit observable rules
Inputs, outputs, state and scope of an operation
Acceptance condition versus caller precondition; postconditions and invariants
Decision tables with mutually exclusive and exhaustive rows for the stated domain
Equivalence classes, boundary values, counterexamples and multi-error priority
Failure preserves named business values while diagnostic output is allowed
Requirement-derived expected results separated from actual execution evidence
engineering_extension: Requirement and case identifiers with version traceability
Parameterized limit changes do not necessarily change validator logic
IM acceptance, durability, per-device receipt and read events require distinct contracts and evidence

new_local_state_model.successful_update: only when input valid and old count 0..9; count+1, lastAccepted=body, preserve draft
new_local_state_model.invalid_initial_state: outside 0..10 returns BAD_STATE after valid input; rejection preserves the bad value and is not repair
new_local_state_model.scope: single sequential local operation; no general concurrency/transaction guarantee

next_steps: 10.02 test methods after its syntax prerequisites are taught
upstream_inspection: Only SendMsg control flow at pinned server commit; factual summary supplied to generator, repository not imported as knowledge base.
validation: Static document checks and manual derivation only; no Go program execution, compilation, tests or site build.
